files.role: the phase itself: preflight, marker, production, result
the wrapper the workflow calls, with the read-back rewired
the workflow that dispatches the two replicas and compares them
the gate that has to pass before any of the above runs
the frozen producer helper the phase hashes its outputs with
the read-back consumer that judges the produced root disk, bound to the successor source lock
the gate that holds that consumer to exactly one lock

frozenBefore: the preflight and the production of this attempt
onMismatch: abort.  A digest here that no longer matches its file means the producer changed after it was sealed, and the attempt does not run on a producer nobody registered.

supersedes.whatItStillRecords: the bytes that produced the third attempt.  It is not re-sealed over the corrected ones, because a seal re-pointed after the fact would claim to have frozen something that never ran and the failure it belongs to would stop being reconstructible from it.

whatIsNewHere: The read-back consumer and its gate are sealed alongside the producer.  The third attempt is what happens when the thing that judges the image is outside the seal: the wrapper called the predecessor's consumer, which reads the predecessor's source lock, and no pin anywhere noticed that a successor image was being measured against the wrong generation's baseline.  A producer that is sealed without its judge is only half sealed.
whatIsNotClaimed: that this producer has run under this authority even once
whyThisIsASeparateRecord: the module pins the authority's digest, so the authority cannot pin the module's.  Sealing the producer in a record that points at the authority, and that nothing points back at, keeps both statements checkable without either having to be written twice.
writtenAfter: the read-back correction was merged, the fourth authority was written and the module was repointed at it, and this gate was final -- so every digest below is the file as it stands and none of them is allowed to have drifted
